item.title: Springvale
item.description:
Town on Ardezax, Bow's hometown — a small farming village near the water. The hag's lair lies in the woods between Springvale and Oakhurst.[1] The town has a general store, a leather worker, a forge, merchant stalls, and an inn, and its farms supply the region.
Under King Aldric Stormborn of Ardezax, who has been demanding extra rations from the small towns. The Royal Guard took Therian about a year ago and have been hunting Bow.[2]
The town was later overrun from within: villagers — Alden among them — transformed into mind flayers and intellect devourers, several killed and children infected, leaving Springvale a ruin the party fled.[3][4]Unknown
The town's inn and tavern, run by the dwarf Roderick Stonehand. Small enough that the party filled all its rooms; it serves dwarven fire whiskey and "dragon fire chili." The party left Clara to rest here.[5]
The farm supplying Springvale's milk and cattle, worked by Alden Caldwell and Mrs. Caldwell. the party left the children rescued from Old Mother Salt here with 50 gold, and Grimgil cast plant growth to double its harvest.[6] That night Alden Caldwell was found transformed into a mind flayer as the children began to turn.[7]
The farmhouse where Bow was raised by Therian. It sat empty for about a year after Therian's arrest until Grimgil magically repaired it during the party's visit.[8]

item.title: Aldric Stormborn
item.description:
King of Ardezax and one of the three leaders of the cult of the Absolute.[1]
He has grown increasingly tyrannical, taken to calling himself Navadjimon, and has put a bounty on Bow, who is wanted dead by the crown.[2]
Bow is in fact his illegitimate son, secretly raised on a Springvale farm by the officer Therian on the king's orders before the paranoid king turned on them both.[3] He had Therian imprisoned in Bruxar and came in person to watch his interrogation — something he never does.[4] He has since left the capital with a couple hundred Royal Guards, spreading the Absolute's new faith across the continent.[5]

item.title: Bruxar
item.description:
A city in Ardezax with a teleportation circle, and home to the Iron accord's headquarters, Hammerpost. The party was teleported here from Drusburgh by Darius Veynar, disguising Bow and Grimgil as horses to slip past the guards who hunt Bow.[1] While there they visited the local chapter of the Gilded Fangs seeking a hag's weakness.
As the king's capital, Bruxar is where corrupt king Aldric Stormborn reigns. By the party's return the city had fallen under the Absolute: every other temple closed, food short, the slums restless, and the paranoid king gone off with a couple hundred Royal Guards.[2][3] Silverwick, a cleric of Selûne worshipping in secret, treated the party outside the walls.
The city holds a Crown District of noble estates — where the advisor Marquet keeps a home — and adjacent Iron Quarters of barracks, armories, and the dungeon.[4] The party infiltrated the barracks dungeon in search of Therian, freeing a former captain, Roderick Vale, and an imprisoned high priestess of Selûne before being ambushed by mind flayers in a torture room below.[5][6]

item.title: Therian Blackwood
item.description:
Bow's father, from the continent of Ardezax.[1] Bow knows him only through recovered memories and dreams — he once guesses the name as "Tharion" — and he appears in a vision of Bow's childhood cottage.[2]
A high-ranking army officer, Therian secretly raised Bow — the illegitimate son of King Aldric Stormborn — on the farmhouse at the king's own orders.[3] The Royal Guard took him about a year ago while hunting Bow, leaving the farmhouse empty.[4] A divination confirmed he was still alive and could be found.[5]
He was held and interrogated in the Bruxar dungeon — the king himself came once to watch, something he never does — before being taken out; his name is now struck from the prisoner registry, whether moved, executed, or transferred is unknown.[6][7]Status: Unknown — no longer held in Bruxar; alive as of the last divination.

item.title: Clara
item.description:
Someone important from Jaden's past, tied to his guilt over an event from when he was a captive of Old Mother Salt.
She is kept in the hag's hut with her mouth sewn shut; Jaden recognized her there and tried to apologize.[1]
When Old Mother Salt died the magic sealing Clara's mouth broke and Jaden revealed himself as the boy who once escaped, coaxing her out of the woods.[2] Overnight she began shifting toward the hag's own form — growing taller and lankier — as something fey took root in her.[3] The transformation resisted dispel magic and holy water, but Eldil's remove curse finally settled her form back toward normal.[4]
She dreams of a normal life — a house, a bakery — and chose to stay behind and keep Bow's repaired farmhouse rather than travel on, though she has since grown about an inch taller with a white crust around her mouth.[5]
Status: Alive, living at the Blackwood farmhouse in Springvale.

item.title: Old Mother Salt
item.description:
Called Old Mother Salt because she is good in moderation, deadly in too large of a dose.She was first suspected of causing the vanishings in Drusburgh, but those turned out to be the work of the False Hydra in the sewers — the hag's meddling proved to be a separate matter.[1] Her own trade is bargains and stolen children: she abducts children (leaving salt at the scene) and speaks to her marks through mirrors and dreams.[2]
Her lair is a sunken hut in the swampy woods between Springvale and Oakhurst, hidden by illusion; those who deal with her forget the way there.[3] She took Koreck, holds Clara with her mouth sewn shut, once made Jaden eat Toby as a boy, and has bound Eldil in a pact demanding Jaden in exchange for his soul.
Beneath her hut lay a gallery of her past bargains and a workshop; her most-hated thing — her anathema — proved to be children's laughter, held in a music box.[4] Her shipping papers exposed a child-trafficking network moving caged children to Caldaren, Drusburgh, and Grey Harbour.[5]
The party stormed her lair, cut down her flesh-servants and a coven of lesser hags, and completed the anathema ritual to make her mortal. Bow's arrow struck the true hag down and Dryz's ritual dragged her fleeing mist into the music box, box and hag crumbling to dust together — killing her for good.[6] Her death broke the swamp's illusion and freed Clara and the caged children.Status: Dead.

item.title: Session 36 (Retreat)
item.description:
[0:04:52] Silverwick, the secret Selûne cleric, introduces Zeenayis Oakenfell — a fungus druid freed from a mind flayer ship who feels the party's infection through his mycelium "bonds beneath the earth." Sharing their hatred of the Absolute, he throws in with the party.
[0:09:30] Still recovering in the outskirts and slums of Bruxar — exhausted and near-broke — the party fixes its aim: reach the castle dungeons and find Bow's father Therian while corrupt king Aldric Stormborn is away with some three hundred elite guards.
[0:17:02] Grimgil remembers the animal-messenger letter he sent last session and reads Marquet's reply, carried back by raven: the king's advisor seems willing to help and agrees to meet on his own terms.
[0:20:04] Over three days Grimgil scouts the locked-down city as animals — a pigeon slipping down office chimneys, a mouse in the barracks. He confirms the castle is lightly guarded with the king gone, every faith but the Absolute is banned by decree, Marquet keeps an estate in the Crown District, and the barracks dungeon holds a few dozen prisoners — but Therian appears in no council record.
[0:35:48] They plan the break-in: Bow shaves and crops his hair to beat the wanted posters, and the group enters as travelers on a supply run, their cover a hunt for rare exotic mushrooms for Zeenayis Oakenfell.
[0:43:35] The infiltration takes shape — Dryz will raise a commotion to pull the guards while the others slip in as rats through a tunnel Zeenayis Oakenfell shapes from the stone.
[1:01:50] Inside the dungeon, an invisible Dryz commands and lulls the corridor guard into a ten-minute sleep, Jaden works the locked door open.
[1:05:57] At the guard's registry they find Therian's name crossed out — moved, executed, or transferred; he is no longer held here. Two other names stand out: former barracks captain Roderick Vale and the imprisoned high priestess of Selûne.
[1:09:59] They open Roderick Vale's cell. Once captain of the barracks, he was jailed for pressing too hard on the city's crooked food supply. Told plainly that the king is part of the corruption that buried him, he is shaken but unsurprised.
[1:23:45] They also free the high priestess of Selûne, imprisoned for openly defying the king's forced Absolute faith and still rallying the other prisoners from her cell. Both freed captives are urged to lie low in the slums rather than go public.
[1:29:45] Roderick offers to guide them deeper: a torture room and a ledger of interrogations lie below, where Therian was questioned — the king himself came once to watch, something he never does. [1:34:03] The last level opens into a slaughterhouse — makeshift tables, hospital cots, body parts and blood everywhere — and the party is ambushed. A mind flayer and a pack of intellect devourers fall on them in the dark.
[1:41:50] The fight turns desperate: Repeatedly grappled and stunned, Bow sharpshoots, Jaden knifes from invisibility, Zeenayis Oakenfell summons beasts and fiery shackles, and Dryz shoves the aberrations with telekinesis.
[1:48:58] The mind flayer seizes Roderick Vale in its tentacles and tears out his brain — the freed captain, who had led them down, is killed at once.
[2:15:09] The mind flayer wraps Grimgil in its tentacles and devours his brain, killing him outright — no save.
[2:22:54] Zeenayis's confusion finally breaks the aberrations, and the party grinds the mind flayer and its devourers down.
[2:53:39] Nothing can save Grimgil: the freed priestess can't reach him inside the one-minute revivify window, and with his brain consumed it won't take.

item.title: Session 35
item.description:
[0:06:37] Picking up mid-fight from last session, Grimgil returns as a giant eagle to find the rest of the party bloodied and near death in the Caldwell farmhouse; Eldil burns Aura of Vitality and Lay on Hands to haul everyone back to their feet as the last attackers fall.
[0:11:12] Still in the ruined farmhouse in the dead of night with no long rest, the party debates the two surviving children and concludes it may be drawing the transformations itself — "we're the danger here" — and leaves the kids hidden with Mrs. Caldwell rather than take them. A short walk through the village confirms the worst: the attackers were the villagers themselves, partially and unevenly transformed into illithids and brain-like devourers, several now dead.
[0:22:22] Back at Bow's repaired house they check on Clara — still herself, but with a residue of white crusted around her mouth and grown "about an inch taller."
[0:25:31] Grimgil casts speak with animals and tries to hire a night-watch owl with jerky, but the deal falls through and the owl flies off. The party lights a fire, sets watches, and finally takes its long rest; come morning it brews tea from the plants Grimgil's plant-growth ritual revived, then heads into Springvale to learn why illithids keep erupting wherever it goes.
[0:44:19] The "investigation" is quick: villagers report no outside attackers — the transformations came from within. Eldil's detect evil and good pings an aberration signature on a closed crate at a market stall.
[0:53:38] The crate matches the hag's smuggling crates, and something is moving inside. Grimgil casts reduce and stuffs it into the bag of holding while wary villagers eye them as thieves and the party spots wanted posters of Bow; Bow agrees they will pose as bounty-and-captive if the guards close in.
[1:04:56] Weighing its three leads — the Absolute cult (their only tadpole connection), the hag's crates, and Bow's missing father Therian — the party settles on the king's city of Bruxar, some seven days east, where corrupt king Aldric Stormborn (Bow's biological father and an Absolute leader) reigns and may also hold Therian.
[1:17:37] Grimgil ritual-casts divination, asking the earth whether they will find Therian in Bruxar; the omen is cryptic — they might not find what they seek even if they find him: lied to, dead, or corrupted.
[1:26:07] Clara chooses to stay behind and keep Bow's farmhouse rather than adventure. With no memory of home or family beyond her fellow captives, she and Jaden — who knew her in the hag's cages — share a quiet, conflicted goodbye.
[1:35:52] On the road Jaden has Grimgil send an animal-messenger letter to Marquet, the king's right hand and a hoped-for ally, to be answered once they draw near Bruxar.
[1:43:13] By the third day of travel Jaden, Bow, and Eldil fall ill — exhausted, half-speed, disadvantage on everything — while Grimgil, who alone escaped the frog-creatures' stuns, stays healthy. Nothing they try (detect magic, lesser restoration, remove disease, foraging, repeated divinations) touches it.
[1:54:52] They finally open the reduced crate: rotten fish sprouting tentacles, corrupted and undead, stamped from a fishing outfit out of Grey Harbour. Burning it with wall of fire leaves a medallion bearing the Absolute's insignia in the ash — tying the tadpole plague to Absolute-run fish shipments.
[2:06:35] A fresh divination reveals the sickness is "eating them from the inside out." Piecing it together, the three realize the farm's stunning frog-creatures infected them during the fight — a second kind of tadpole layered over their Netherese-touched ones.
[2:09:31] Reaching Bruxar, they find the king's city locked down under the Absolute: temples closed, the paranoid king gone with hundreds of Crown's guards, food short and the slums restless. Grimgil slips inside as a bird, then a cat, and hires Silverwick — a cleric of Selûne worshipping in secret — to treat the dying party outside the walls, shaking off slum thieves by claiming rabies and, once, by becoming a massive dire wolf.
[2:39:53] Silverwick's own divination pins the cure to remove curse. Over the casting he fills them in on Bruxar: the Absolute's grip on the closed temples runs all the way to the throne, the king has grown stricter and more selfish and left the city with a couple hundred Royal Guards, and hungry unrest in the slums is being quashed fast.
[2:56:14] Silverwick lifts the curse — the implanted aberration eggs die before their twenty-four-hour hatch, which would otherwise have killed each host and birthed an illithid. Cured but drained and near-broke, the party resolves to lie low in Bruxar. To be continued.

item.title: Session 34
item.description:
[0:19:54] Picking up from the raid, the party storms the Caldwell farm in the dead of night. Jaden, invisible in the dark, opens fire on Alden Caldwell — now a mind flayer feeding on a child — landing six hits in the first round.
[0:21:45] The threats become clear: the mind flayer that was Alden Caldwell, and several intellect devourers — brains on four legs that stun their prey — crawling from the skulls of the children left here.
[0:39:47] Eldil arrives late and is quickly restrained and stunned. The mind flayer whispers for him not to "forget the promises that were offered" to him, but he shrugs it off — the promises, he says, were bullshit. [0:48:19] Reddish, clawed frog-like creatures pour into the fight, while the intellect devourers latch onto the front line and lock them down with stuns.
[0:59:05] The mind flayer unleashes pulsing waves of psychic energy, battering Dryz and Jaden with mind blasts as blood runs from their ears.
[2:03:04] After two rounds of setup, Eldil cuts loose with his Radiant Consumption and a devastating divine smite — roughly 120 damage — finally turning the tide. [2:18:20] Even as enemies fall, a fresh mind flayer arrives to replace the dead, and during the chaos one mind flayer tears open a strange rift and escapes.
[2:28:07] The party clears the farmhouse at last — Bow's arrows, Dryz's telekinesis, and Eldil's smites finishing the attackers — but the wider village is already overrun.
[2:30:51] The cost is grim: of the five children the party left at the farm, three are dead with their brains consumed, and Alden Caldwell is dead. Mrs. Caldwell is unconscious but alive; a goodberry and Eldil's lay on hands revive her, and they warn her to stay hidden and quiet with the surviving children. [2:35:52] Shaken, the party wrestles with guilt — are their own tadpole-infected heads triggering these transformations wherever they travel? Reflecting, they can't be certain: it has happened near them before, but not always, and "weird things are happening with mind flayers" everywhere right now.
[2:38:56] They tie the attack back to the hag's ledger — the "pearls," the coded Black Tide, Salt Moon and Widow's Storm shipments, and Grey Harbour — wondering if the frog-creatures hatched from smuggled eggs, and recalling the aberrations once seen transforming near Sylvanus Grove.
[2:40:27] Rather than push into the ruined town, they resolve to slip out, camp for the night, and scout the port at Grey Harbour in the morning — still bent on reaching Baldur’s Gate — and head back to Bow's house to regroup with Clara. To be continued.

item.title: Session 33
item.description:
[0:05:03] Morning at camp after the long rest. Overnight Clara kept shifting toward the hag's form, so the party debates whether she is "going evil." Eldil casts detect evil and good and finds she isn't fully fey, but something fey is taking root in her — she is in transition. [0:08:52] They try to halt the change: dispel magic (no effect), holy water, and protection from evil and good — nothing stops it.
[0:12:39] Grimgil walks into the forest and ritual-casts divination — cinnamon burned, his blood poured into the earth — asking whether Clara is an evil threat. The omen is cryptic: she is becoming a hag, but "even the incarnation of evil isn't necessarily a threat to you."
[0:20:39] The party weighs killing and revivifying her to strip the curse versus letting her live. They note that slaying Old Mother Salt already lifted the swamp's illusion and that the neck-marks and curses she left them are fading.
[0:25:59] Questioned about her plans, Clara dreams of a normal life — a house, a bakery — but insists the hag isn't truly dead and expects to be caged again soon; Jaden conjures a minor illusion of the hag to test her reaction.
[0:32:04] Eldil casts remove curse on Clara. Between that and the morning's efforts her form settles back toward normal and the fogginess leaves her, though the party stays wary.
[0:35:06] Jaden ritual-casts animal messenger, sending a sparrow with a letter to his father Gustave.
[0:39:09] With the illusion gone the forest is far smaller than remembered. Bow recalls the local geography and the party settles on Springvale, Bow's hometown, to leave the rescued children rather than Oakhurst or Bruxar; Grimgil scouts from the air to find the fastest way out of the woods.
[1:01:16] Two days' travel later they near Springvale. Bow is sent ahead as a sparrow to scout: the town is guarded but there are no wanted posters of him on display and no imminent danger.
[1:08:13] At the inn, the Grubby Griffin, dwarf innkeeper Roderick Stonehand recognizes Bow. He reveals that Bow's father Therian was taken by the Royal Guard about a year ago and the family farmhouse has sat empty since — and that the guards were hunting Bow too.
[1:21:26] Roderick sends them to the Caldwell farm to house the children. Mrs. Caldwell takes them in, and the party leaves the kids plus 50 gold; they keep Clara to rest at the inn. The Caldwells mention the king has been demanding extra rations from the small towns.
[1:29:48] Bow visits his father's ransacked house and recounts his last memory: mercenaries and Royal Guard came, Therian told him to run, and he fell unconscious and woke near the party. Grimgil magically repairs the house with stone shape and controlled flame.
[1:44:50] Grimgil ritual-casts divination again: Bow's father is alive and can be found.
[1:53:10] Grimgil casts plant growth over the Caldwell farmland (an eight-hour ritual) to double the year's harvest, helping the village meet the king's rations; Bow restocks metal-shafted arrows at the forge.
[1:58:41] Reading the hag's shipping papers, the party finds a ledger of crates of children bound for Caldaren (the largest shipment), Drusburgh, and Grey Harbour, with coded dates — evidence of a child-trafficking network.
[2:00:31] A letter from Therian hidden in Bow's pack, read alongside the papers, reveals that Bow is the illegitimate son of King Aldric Stormborn, secretly raised on the farm on the king's orders by Therian, a high-ranking army officer. The king has grown paranoid — "whispers into corridors grow louder... he sees threats and shadows that may not even exist, and I have become one of those shadows for him" — and now wants Bow dead or alive, possibly tied to The Absolute. The party resolves to investigate Grey Harbour and eventually return to Baldur’s Gate.
[2:22:00] That night the party keeps watch in the repaired house. On his watch Bow hears screaming from the neighboring Caldwell farm.
[2:29:22] Grimgil polymorphs into a giant eagle and the party flies over: Mrs. Caldwell lies unconscious on the porch, and inside they find Alden Caldwell transformed into a mind flayer and feeding, while the rescued children are being infected and turning too. Initiative is rolled. To be continued.

item.title: Session 32
item.description:
[0:04:57] the party recaps last session: they beat the children and the sewn-mouth woman (Clara), searched the hut, descended into the hag's underground workshop, and identified the children's-laughter music box as her anathema. Jaden stands in the salt circle holding the box, waiting for Dryz to begin the three-round ritual, while Eldil recalls his private end-of-session vision of Manuil taking a religious symbol and shattering it.
[0:12:16] Combat resumes at the top of initiative. The hag floods the room as a swarm of identical copies, and only one is real — the party has to shoot through the illusions to find her, each arrow passing harmlessly through a false image before it vanishes.
[0:17:22] The hag casts hypnotic pattern, charming and incapacitating Dryz and Jaden (speed zero) until someone wakes them or they take damage; Bow fires to snap them out. [0:25:13] The hag lashes out with spectral claws that knock party members prone for heavy damage, and curses those she marks with her Witch Strike — disadvantage on everything and no reactions until the curse ends.
[0:44:53] A counterspell duel breaks out: the hag counterspells Dryz's counterspell, so he answers with a quickened psychic lance and a twinned firebolt to keep the pressure on.
[1:09:13] The hag's tongue-twister curse lands on Grimgil: he can no longer cast spells with verbal components, and everything he says comes out as its opposite — his command to his wolf to "attack" leaves it doing nothing at all.
[1:13:01] The hag hits terrifyingly hard, one area effect dealing 42 damage; Grimgil, Jaden, and later Bow are all knocked unconscious, and the fight teeters on the edge of a total-party wipe.
[1:15:56] the party realizes they must not kill her before the ritual finishes or she will simply return, so they focus on keeping everyone standing — Grimgil's goodberries and healing words — while Dryz holds the three rounds of casting.
[1:27:37] Bloodied, the hag offers a truce — "I still have things to offer you... let's stop this nonsense, we're fighting the same enemy" — but Bow refuses and looses an arrow.
[1:29:02] Bow's arrow passes clean through her mouth; the real hag collapses into a cloud of dust and lingering mist that tries to flee.
[1:32:41] Dryz completes the ritual: the fleeing mist is dragged back into the music box, and box and mist crumble to dust together — Old Mother Salt is dead for good. As she dies, her half-sunken house begins to sink into the swamp.
[1:37:31] Racing the rising water, the party grabs a desk of scattered notes (possible intel), frees the caged children — Grimgil smashing locks, Jaden picking others — and carries out the two unconscious captives and Clara. Grimgil shifts into a polar bear to haul people and clear falling rubble.
[1:44:16] With the hag dead, the magic sealing Clara's sewn mouth breaks; Jaden wakes her with a goodberry. She is terrified and disbelieving, certain it is another of the hag's tricks.
[1:48:29] Out on the shore as the house sinks, Jaden reveals himself as the boy who once escaped and gently tells Clara it is finally over. Grimgil takes the form of a white warhorse to carry the freed children, and Jaden persuades Clara to follow the party out of the woods.
[1:57:54] the party travels a day to the forest's edge, recovers their five horses, and makes camp; the woods already feel less cursed, with distant birdsong returning. Around the fire Eldil and Jaden share a rare emotional moment about what comes next.
[2:04:40] Plans take shape: eventually kill the corrupt king Aldric Stormborn of Ardezax, get intel on his advisor Marquet (a hoped-for ally), and hunt Eldil's brother Manuil — though the deal meant to reveal Manuil's location only bought "half a soul for half an answer." Their main goal remains returning to Baldur’s Gate to get the tadpoles out of their heads. Jaden plans to send an Animal Messenger letter to his father Gustave in the morning, and the party debates where to bring the rescued children — perhaps the Temple of Selûne in Drusburgh — worried that many were sold by their own parents.
[2:20:38] Through the night watches Bow and Jaden notice Clara's body slowly changing — growing taller and lankier, taking on the shape of the hag's true form — while the fading mark on their necks still prickles and burns. Jaden wonders if she could be the same race as him. The party resolves to try dispelling whatever is on her in the morning as they take a long rest and level up. To be continued.

item.title: Session 31
item.description:
[0:08:15] With the hag fled and the children and Clara subdued, the party binds the unconscious captives (Bow ties them with fifty feet of rope) and sets out to find the anathema and kill the hag in her own home.
[0:17:45] Dryz casts detect magic to sweep the house. In the bedroom the party finds two magical tomes (wizard's spellbooks), the kitchen cupboards hold glowing vials, and the children's room still radiates enchantment magic. They pocket the spellbooks and the potions.
[0:26:22] the party hunts for a way down. Grimgil tears the bedroom apart searching, but no trapdoor turns up, and the doors and windows are all locked shut — they realize the hag is keeping them penned inside.
[0:37:57] Eldil goes back to the kitchen cupboard the sewn-mouth woman (Clara) crawled out of and finds a dugout tunnel hidden behind it, sloping underground.
[0:38:29] the party descends. The passage stinks of salt and swamp; Eldil recognizes it as the same underground the hag once stranded him in.
[0:39:01] The tunnel opens into a long gallery arranged like a museum — effigies of the hag's past deals, each one twisted into a curse. Among them is Eldil's own recent bargain to bring Jaden, and Gustave, Jaden's father, who dealt to "get rid of a monster to find his daughter" and is shown cradling a dead girl.
[0:54:37] Past the gallery the party reaches the hag's workshop — a workbench rather than a shrine, ringed with cupboards, books, ingredients and locked chests. A faint cackling laugh and whispers drift on the air.
[1:05:13] In the corners lie the decomposing bodies of children. One has been grotesquely stretched; Grimgil recognizes it as a shapeshifting field experiment, and Bow is shaken by the sight.
[0:57:55] the party recalls the ritual from the anathema lore: a circle drawn with something that has an affinity to the hag, with her most-hated thing held at the center, completed by a ritual caster over three rounds to make her mortal for ten. They settle on salt, and Jaden's blood for his affinity to her.
[1:09:47] Searching the workbench they turn up trinkets — a shoe, a doll, a wooden horse, bundles of hair, jars of eyeballs and teeth, fingers, a mirror, and a music box. Jaden recognizes the mirror as the one a stall merchant once used to show him Clara.
[1:16:08] Bow winds the music box: instead of music it pours out the sound of pure children's laughter and blows out every light in the room. the party concludes laughter is the anathema, just as Koreck warned that Mother Salt hates it.
[1:18:39] Combat begins as gangly, hound-like flesh servants of the hag pour in from the corridors. the party fights them off.
[1:43:16] While the others fight, draws the circle in salt; Jaden slices his hand with his rapier to add his blood, and stands in the center with the music box. They agree not to begin the three-round casting until the hag herself appears.
[1:49:54] Smaller hags — a coven working with Old Mother Salt — spring from the tunnels, frightening several of the party (especially Bow). the party cuts down the servants and the mini-hags one by one.
[1:56:06] Dryz begins the ritual as the party downs the last of the coven.
[2:10:00] As the session closes, Old Mother Salt herself appears, pouring in from all five corridors at once. In the same instant a vision flashes to Eldil: he sees Manuil take a religious symbol in his hand and shatter it, though its meaning escapes him. To be continued.

item.title: Valient Amber
item.description:
Merrick Thorn's ship, out of Black Tide Bay. The party sailed it from Longtooth Island toward Drusburgh on Ardezax, a voyage during which a kraken attacked and killed most of the crew.[1] Its quartermaster, Tessa, had earlier vanished in Drusburgh.
A kraken attacks the Valient Amber (Session 23)↩︎

item.title: Cloak of Elvenkind
item.description:
A magic cloak looted from goblin corpses inside Mount Dalgan.[1]
The party loots a Cloak of Elvenkind (Session 14)↩︎

item.title: Oath Bow
item.description:
A magic bow looted from the hobgoblin Dror Ragzlin after the battle in Celadon.[1] It became Jaden's signature weapon, which he wields through the Colosseum of Chaos and beyond; he later wrapped its tip in mistletoe dipped in blood.
The party loots the Oath Bow from Dror Ragzlin (Session 8)↩︎

item.title: Gith Crèche
item.description:
A githyanki crèche near where the party first landed on Longtooth Island. La’zael told them it holds a device called a Zaith'isk that can remove a tadpole — a possible cure.[1]Githyanki.Unknown
The Zaith'isk, a device said to purge the tadpole parasite. The party has not yet visited the crèche.
The party learns the crèche's Zaith'isk can remove tadpoles (Session 1)↩︎

item.title: Broken Bridge
item.description:
A bridge on Longtooth Island on the route to Frila, destroyed by goblins and shrouded in a mist that drains the magical energy of any spellcaster who breathes it. The party crossed it on Grimgil's conjured giant owls.[1]
The party crosses the mist-covered, goblin-destroyed Broken Bridge (Session 16)↩︎

item.title: Balg
item.description:
part of the dead three
Once an assassin and a charmer, he took over the portfolio of Murder when Jergal gave up his throne and divided its powers.[1]
Jergal gifts the portfolios; Balg takes Murder (Session 0)↩︎

item.title: Myrkul
item.description:
part of the dead three
God of death; his symbol is an upright triangle topped with a skull.[1] The necromancer Malkavor Ardin made a pact with him, plotting to sacrifice Nilas Orelian's soul to open a portal that would loose death upon Frila.[2]
Myrkul's symbol is an upright triangle with a skull (Session 19)↩︎
Malkavor's journal reveals his deal with Myrkul (Session 18)↩︎

item.title: Selûne
item.description:
Goddess of the moon, the benevolent twin of Shar.[1] A temple to her stands in Celadon,[2] and another in Drusburgh, led by head priestess Lisandra Valora with the priest Nyx.[3]
Selûne is named as Shar's moon-goddess twin (Session 0)↩︎
A temple of Selûne stands in Celadon (Session 10)↩︎
Lisandra Valora heads the Selûne temple in Drusburgh (Session 25)↩︎

item.title: Shar
item.description:
The Faerûnian goddess of darkness and night, the malevolent twin of Selûne, goddess of the moon. She takes pleasure in corrupting Aasimar to sow discord in their ranks. Shadowheart bears her symbol and worships her.[1]
Shar is described as Shadowheart's dark goddess, twin of Selûne (Session 0)↩︎

item.title: True Soul
item.description:
True Souls are individuals marked and empowered by the Absolute and counted among its chosen. Those who manifest its power are named among them: Erru fled believing Grimgil had become one after he dominated her,[1] the commander Minthara urged the party to stop fighting and "turn to the Absolute" as true souls,[2] and Da Bawss insisted their power had been granted by the Absolute.[3]
Erru reports Grimgil is a True Soul of the Absolute (Session 2)↩︎
Minthara calls the party true souls (Session 9)↩︎
Da Bawss says the party's power came from the Absolute (Session 12)↩︎

item.title: Toby
item.description:
Someone important from Jaden's past.
The hag made Jaden eat him as a kid, and he used one of his bones to escape. His spirit still lingers in the hag's house, where Jaden recognized him.[1]
Jaden recognizes Toby's spirit in the hag's house (Session 29)↩︎

item.title: Koreck
item.description:
A small child and the latest target of Old Mother Salt. He comes from near where the hag lives, where it is said anyone who leaves always returns.
The party left him on the hallowed ground of the temple of Selûne in Drusburgh for safety, but the hag took him anyway. They later found him among the ghost-children in her house, no longer himself.[1]
Koreck is found among the hag's ghost-children (Session 30)↩︎

item.title: Nyx
item.description:
A priest of the temple of Selûne in Drusburgh. He tried to lift the mark Old Mother Salt left on Jaden with a remove curse, but it failed.[1]
Nyx fails to remove Jaden's mark (Session 25)↩︎

item.title: Thomas Aquinous
item.description:
A member of the Iron accord, working from its archives in Drusburgh. He helped the party research how to kill a hag, producing a book from Baldur’s Gate that describes the ritual to make the hag mortal using her Anathema, and took their testimony so the Iron accord could investigate.[1]
Thomas helps the party research killing a hag (Session 28)↩︎

item.title: Khaga
item.description:
UnknownStopped her from punishing Arabella but put Grimgil and Eldil in jail [1]Antagonistic
A harsh figure of authority in Sylvanus Grove. Halsin later stripped her of her title.[2]Alive
Session 2↩︎
Halsin strips Khaga of her title (Session 16)↩︎

item.title: Cazador
item.description:
The being who held Astarion as a thrall for a thousand years, under a curse Astarion accepted on death's door. Astarion was freed only when a tadpole was implanted in him aboard the ship, and believes Cazador still wants him dead.[1] Astarion warned the party never to accept Cazador's help.[2]
Astarion fears Cazador wants him dead (Session 17)↩︎
Astarion warns against accepting Cazador's help (Session 17)↩︎

item.description:
GoblinWatched the party's fights in the Colosseum of Chaos from his own box beside Priestess Glut, and claimed their power had been granted by the Absolute.[1]
Present at the summoning ritual deep in Mount Dalgan alongside Priestess Glut.[2]Enemy
King of the goblins, ruling from their capital Trixie.[3] Blorg went to Trixie hoping to overthrow him.
Unknown — last seen at the erupting Mount Dalgan.

item.title: Blixby
item.description:
Goblin inspector who runs the Colosseum of Chaos games in Trixie. He forces contestants to become "the Absolute's Chosen," his shamans laying a wisdom curse on them before the first round.[1] Between bouts he shackles the fighters, and after their victories he escorted the party out of the colosseum.
Blixby forces the party to become the Absolute's Chosen (Session 11)↩︎

item.title: Darius Veynar
item.description:
Dryz's mentor, who trained him as an investigator with the Crowns guard in Drusburgh.
He rewarded the party for slaying the False Hydra, warned them that King Aldric Stormborn was turning tyrannical and had marked Bow for death, and asked them to help stabilize the city.[1] He also mentioned that Dryz's parents had not been seen in some time.[2] He later teleported the party from Drusburgh to Bruxar.[3]
Darius debriefs the party and warns about the king (Session 27)↩︎
Darius notes Dryz's parents have gone missing (Session 27)↩︎
Darius teleports the party to Bruxar (Session 28)↩︎

item.title: Astarion
item.description:
Elf (undead)Found in Frila posing as a living elf while secretly undead, quietly helping the town's guards.[1]
At first believed the party were assassins sent by Cazador.[2]
Later joined the party, sailing with them on the Valient Amber, though he stayed out of the kraken fight.[3]Ally
Like the party, Astarion was aboard the ship and had a tadpole implanted in him — which freed him from Cazador, whose thrall he had been for a thousand years after accepting a curse on death's door. He warned Eldil never to accept Cazador's help.[4]Alive (undead). Traveling with the party.
An undead elf is found in Frila (Session 17)↩︎
Astarion thinks the party are Cazador's assassins (Session 17)↩︎
Astarion sits out the kraken attack (Session 23)↩︎
Astarion reveals he was Cazador's thrall, freed by the tadpole (Session 17)↩︎

item.title: Shadowheart
item.description:
UnknownMet the party at the Chapel Ruins, where she was trying to reach the artifact; when it attuned to the party instead, she told them to bring it to Baldur’s Gate and wait for her there.[1]
Reunited with the party at Black Tide Bay and joined the voyage on the Valient Amber, though she and Astarion stayed out of the fight when a kraken attacked the ship.[2]Ally (uneasy)
A worshipper of Shar, the goddess of darkness; the Nightsong is something important to her.[3]
Alive. Traveling with the party toward Ardezax.
Shadowheart tells the party to bring the Artifact to Baldur's Gate (Session 0)↩︎
Shadowheart and Astarion sit out the kraken attack (Session 23)↩︎
Halsin notes the Nightsong matters to Shadowheart (Session 16)↩︎

item.title: Gale
item.description:
HumanMet the party at the Crashed Nautiloid, already infected with a tadpole like them, and pointed them toward the Chapel Ruins and its hidden artifacts.[1]
The party gave him one of their magic items to absorb so he could satiate his "hunger".[2]
Rejoined the party at Black Tide Bay and sailed with them on the Valient Amber, reporting that the tadpole problem is everywhere — even off Longtooth Island — and that the hosts may all transform in a single event.[3]
Explained the Netherese magic protecting the parasite, and the tale of Karsus, the follower of Mystra who forged it trying to overthrow her.[4]AllyA powerful wizard with an unusual affliction: he must consume magic items to feed a "hunger" within him.
Alive. Traveling with the party toward Ardezax.
Gale meets the infected party and points them to the chapel ruins (Session 0)↩︎
The party feeds Gale a magic item (Session 2)↩︎
Gale reports the tadpole problem is everywhere (Session 22)↩︎
Gale explains the Netherese magic and Karsus (Session 22)↩︎

item.title: Session 29
item.description:
The party quickly dispatched of most of the people trying to attack them. Grimgil uses a wild shape to change into a burrowing animal and make a grave for the thieves. Bow takes a moment to regret his swift killing of these desperate people.
The party continues their travels, Jaden and Dryz discuss the vial incident. Grimgil identifies the vial as Wyvern poison, The party continues on their journey to find the hags lair.
The party travels for a few days and get to the woods outside where the hags lair is, there are no signs or indication as to where to go, people who make deals with the hag forget where she lives. Eldil seems to know to enter the woods.
Grimgil tries to speak to a bird to get information on the hags location. the bird has no idea where it might be, but Eldil has a vibe of where he needs to go.
The party have to leave the horses behind as the forest get thicker. as they get deeper the trees start to part and get less dense. Grimgil casts locate creature on Old Mother Salt, he doesn't sense anything yet. The party continues at Eldil's guidance.
The further the party goes into the forest, they notice a distinct lack of birds, Jaden doesn't like the woods. they encounter some small streams, when he was young and Jaden escaped, he escaped from a children's room, into a dining room and a corridor leading to the exterior. Jaden doesn't exactly remember the landscape, it smelled of salt mixed with other foul smell. the terrain was difficult to navigate, he eventually did the revers of the parties trip to outside of the forest.
The party finally arrives to a clearing, Grimgil casts detect magic, and feels illusion magic all around, Dryz tries to invetigate and shatters the illusion, the clearing is actually gross and not green, Dryz informs the party of this and Eldil casts dispel magic on the illusion, but it fails. Jaden manages to see through the illusion. he recognizes the smell.
The party continues onwards in the illusion, the party encounters creatures, they look like sheep under the illusion. Dryz tries to warn Grimgil that it's a beast, but it attacks him. Roll for initiative.
The party manages to dispatch of the the sheep / werewolves, they bandage a few wounds and continue on their way to the hag, walking in water they see a nice cabin / a weird gnarly sunken wooden house.
They need to cross a 40 ft river, Jaden uses fly to carry the party across but they get attacked by a flower before Dryz can be carried accross. Roll for initiative.
The party defeats a swamp creature and approach the hag's hut. Edlil, Grim and Jaden cast protection against good and evil on themselves.
As the party gets near the hut, the door opens with a creak. an old lady exits the hut and addresses the party, thanks them for bringing Jaden and asks the rest of the party what they need, she mentions that we helped her with the false hydra, and offer to make a deal for us to defeat manuil and Karsus to prevent him from coming back and killing Mystra.
The hag modifies the memory of the party except for Grimgil to make them think that leaving Jaden with her is not a bad idea.
Jaden and Grimgil argues with the rest of the party convincing them that they've been deceived, they move in to the hut, Jaden see's the spirit of a small boy wayving at him, Jaden recongnizes him as Toby (The kid the hag made him eat).
The small of salt is strong inside the dimly lit hut, it is a like a tree trunk twisting down into the ground, after about 10 ft in the hut Eldil and Jaden stop.
Eldil finds himself in a chamber from his childhood home, it's candlelit and Manuil is also there, he has a book of magic. "one day brother we'll be more than this, we'll have enough power to make the world bend" he says, and offer the book to Eldil. Eldil refuses the book, glyphs on the book animate and enter Manuil's body and his eyes start to burn with netherese fire. The room crumbles into the location Eldil saw in the vision presented by the Hag.
Jaden finds himself in a dining hall from his childhood home, his parents are there raising a toast to Jaden (Tyll). everything is perfect, a sibling of Jaden tells him to show everyone what he can do. Jaden hesitates and doesn't want to show his family what he can do, his sibling keeps pushing. His siblings turns against him, and call him a monster.
Grimgil finds himself in the smoky cavern of his clans den, Goblin children are laughing and cheering as they bully Grimgil, his parents watch disappointed, telling him he doesn't belong and to leave, the cavern crumbles as jeers echo louder.
Dryz finds himself in a dimly lit cavern, with faint light on the walls, Elir calls out, they are hanging out. Elir asks "We will watch each others backs forever won't we?" Dryz agrees, but suddenly he turns white and screeches, disappearing.
Thimithiel finds himself in a small familiar cottage, with Therian Blackwood, his dad, he sits by the fire. "We're safe here boy, no one will ever hurt you" he says. Shadows appear and crawl across the floor. "you were never safe, you were never wanted" he now says. the door opens with a cold wind, and the king enters and points at Bow "Bastard, Mistake, Hidden thing you should never had drawn breath"

item.title: Session 30
item.description:
The party rolls for initiative to decide in what order the party resolves their simultaneous visions. Grimgil goes first.
Grimgil is in a the cavern from his vison his raptor has turned on him and a swarm of goblin children, Grim casts polymorph on his raptor and attempts to run away, the floating monster amalgam chases and hits Grimgil. Grimgil stops and faces the monster. Grimgil screams about compassion being strength and the monster disappears then gives and emotional speech to his raptor who breaks through and is back on his side
Bow is next: He is in his childhood home facing the king, Bow attempts to talk to the king, he says something, (I didn't hear, tequila shots were happening). The king attacks him. kings guard also enter the room. Bow cocks his bow and attacks, the king lands some blows, telling bow he is a mistake that needs to be corrected. Bow fights and defeats the king. but then the house is on fire, Bow tries to run away and escapes successfully.
Eldil is next: Manuil taunts him, Eldil turns on radiant consumption and fights him. after a hard fought battle, Eldil is victorious and escapes successfully.
Jaden is next: he is still at the table in the family hope, his little sister is taunting him, his dad starts shooting him with a bow and says "what are you really". Jaden shouts "she's lying" very convincingly, his parents leave, all that is left is his sister. Jaden kills his sister and escapes.
Next is Dryz: Elir is in font of him and screeches a dissonant whispers Dryz. Dryz tells the thing that looks like Elir "For what it's worth I solved the mystery" this satisfies Elir who sheds an tear and disappears.
The party wakes up on the swampy floor of the hag's house. They can perceive the ghastly faces of children moving through the area, at the end of a corridor they're are 2 children waiting, one of the children is koreck, he tells the party they taste like choice.
Eldil asks koreck what mother hates, Eldil rolls a 38 on persuasion. At the same time Dryz uses detect thoughts to find out of any deception. Koreck tells Eldil, old Mother salt hates laughter and the little boys don't stick around as long. the little girl is looking at jaden and thinking "one of us, one of us, trapped....".
The little girls tells Jaden "Mother says you are the answer to their question"
Bow explores and finds the kitchen and the area where she kept the children. the party moves and enters the kitchen together. The hag appears in a doorway to the question, she says "come and eat, dinner is ready". Eldil collects some salt from the kitchen, to the protest of Koreck, he believes that whoever enters the kitchen is who they eat next.
As Eldil leaves there is a weird baby hand coming out of the cupboards and a lady with a sown mouth, she shoo's Eldil. Jaden recognizes Clara, he tries to apologize to her, she cries but doesn't how to react to Jaden.
The hag thanks the party for bringing Jaden to her. The party refuses to hand him over. roll for initiative.
During combat Dryz casts suggestion on clara to tell him where the Hag's anathema is, she tells Dryz it is probably in a forbidden room in the depths of her home.
Midway through the combat, the hag runs away and disappears. the party subdues the children and Clara, combat is over.

item.title: Session 10
item.description:
The Party is in front of the town hall after killing Minthara. Jaden heads to the Celadon Barracks, enters the window grabs a hook a rope and a flag of the absolute. Eldil writes the absolute is dead in the ground. The party heads to the sewers, Jaden looks for egg sized garnotte.
Jaden is a sewer expert and helps us move faster through the sewers, a war horn sounds in the city. Grimgil summons a rat familiar and leaves it in the sewers as a lookout. The party jumps out of the sewers and heads to the forest. The beach is rocky, but not egg sized... except for 1 single rock
A goblin spotted the party leaving but seemed more concerned with what was happening inside the city. Grimgil takes control of the rat to investigate the celadon inner city, the source of the horn, the goblins found Minthara's dead body and are regrouping. Grumnack is talking to Rugsog, they discuss going back to Trixie and start heading to Trixie. Arcane eyes left the city first and the goblins followed them.
The Party discusses plans, settle on letting the Goblins filter out of Celadon and then liberating it and looking for information in the city. set up camp in the forest south of the city and rest for the rest of the day. Jaden makes tea, Eldil practices the Pan flute. Grimgil heads into the wilderness to find food, only finds a single bad mushroom and some water. Jaden gives Dryz his headband of Intellect.
Bow goes to the river, dominates a fish and kills it to brings it to camp to eat. The party starts a long rest, during Eldil and Grimgil's watch. Grimgil has a heart to heart with Eldil, possibly effective. Grimgil also asks about his darkness. Eldil only says "he has unfinished business to deal with". and doesn't share more than that. Jaden during his watch sneaks a garnotte in Eldil's bag.
The long rest is over the party is now level 7
Grimgil goes to forage again in the morning and prepares a root, goodberry and squirrel meal for everyone.
Grimgil creates a flying familiar to check out what is happening in Celadon, there is no goblin activity at all in the city. There are signs of battle and more dead goblins in the city. there are no Arcane eyes. The party heads towards Celadon.
At the city gate, it is locked. Eldil throws a grappling on top of the wall and climbs the wall to unlock the gate for the rest of the party.
The party heads straight to the town hall in the inner city, on the way notice plenty of dead goblin Grumnack is one of them. it seems like some of the goblins tried to free themselves from the absolute but it didn't go to well.
In front of the town hall Grimgil casts Detect magic, the party enters the townhall and looks for Maps and documents that might lead to baldur's gate. A map is found, longtooth island is south west, faerun is to the east and north east of longtooth is Ardezax? a bigger island (more details from DM to follow).
In the makeshift prisons the party finds 4 remain civilians, Bow free's them and offers them goodberries, Grimgil talks to one of them, during the same time Eldil casts prayer of healing on them. Theodore Kesington is the mayor of Celadon. one of the other survivors is his wife Evelyn Kisington. The party instructs the mayor to head back to the grove, inform them Celadon is free and safe and bring back the refugees.
Jaden raids the granary to make a large stew for the survivors, Eldil brings the civilians to the temple, Grimgil follows Theodore Kesington and his wife to his home, Grimgil gets a fancy bow.
At the temple (Temple of Selune, there is rubble blocking the crypt so Eldil and Grimgil start removing the rubble. Bow and Dryz start helping a little later. The mayor grabs a magical vial of blood from an office in the crypt and gives it to us and the leaves for the grove
The Party raids the rest of the crypt and finds 500GP of golden objects, 50 GP of diamonds and 50GP of other gems.
The party decides to make their way towards Trixie to rescue Halsin from the Gladiator games.
At a river crossing the Party sets up camp so Grimgil can prepare water walk. at nigth Grimgil tells the party about his childhood. (I was listening so the details are not written, Alex send me a summary if you have one). Jaden shares that he is from Ardezax, so is Dryz. Ardezax is familiar to Bow.
To help Bow find out more about himself, Grimgil uses detect thoughts and dives deeper into his psyche, but does not find any valuable information. He thinks his name is not Bow, but before he met us a tiefling kept calling him Bow.
Dryzfrin is from Misthaven, Jaden grew up Caldaren, Eldil is from western Faerun.
One of the people we rescued (Benjamin) from the approaches us in the middle of the night, tells us he is not feeling well, he stayed in Celadon, he collapses and tentacles sprout from him, Roll for Initiative! Combat Play-by-Play:
Eldil activates his radiant consumption
The tentacle monster opens a portal and hits everyone but Eldil for large amount of damage.
Jaden gets up applies hunter's mark to benjamin, shoots and hit him twice.
Eldil attacks the benjamin twice and hits once.
Bow gets up uses second wind, then shoots the alligators twice and hits once, bloodying it.
The alligators dash to grimgil and Dryz
Dryz uses mind sliver twice on benjamin, forces a legendary resistance use for one, the other fails even with silvery barbs from Dryz and Grimgil.
Grimgil summons his fire spirit and moves behind bow to get cover
Benjamin moves towards Dryz, Eldil hits with an opportunity attack. uses lightning bolt on dryz, bow and grimgil. all three save and take half damage
